The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=2$ the particle is located at the position $x=5.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=9?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=9$ is equal to its position at $t=2$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [2,9].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(9)=x(2)+{\int }_{2}^{9}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(2)=5,$ and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{2}^{9}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=2$ to $t=9.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{2}^{9}v(t)\,\text{d}t=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(9)=5+2=7.
$$

So, the position of the particle at $t=9$ is $x=7.$
